title: Restrict AppConfig to a single instance
description: AppConfig holds application-wide settings in a plain class. It has a public constructor, so any caller can create its own independent instance — each with its own separate state.
hints: Add a private static field of type AppConfig to hold the single instance
Make the constructor private so callers cannot use new AppConfig()
Add a public static getInstance() method that creates the instance on first call and returns it every time
issues: AppConfig can be instantiated freely with new AppConfig()
Each caller gets its own separate config, so changes made in one place are invisible elsewhere
overallGoal: Use the Singleton pattern to ensure AppConfig can only be instantiated once, so all callers share the same instance and configuration state is consistent across the application.
goals: Add a private static AppConfig field to hold the single instance
Make the constructor private so callers cannot use new AppConfig()
Add a public static getInstance() method that lazy-initializes and returns the instance
